landing.heroTitle: Rehabilitation, with a little more support.
landing.heroSubtitle: Follow your prescribed exercises at home with camera-based movement tracking, guided demonstrations, and progress insights designed to support your recovery journey.
landing.previewNote: Interactive component simulation. In live sessions, your device camera estimates joints locally without recording or transmitting raw video frames.
landing.howItWorksSubtitle: A structured, three-step clinical loop designed to assist proper exercise execution at home.
landing.step1Desc: Access assigned protocols tailored to your condition, complete with targeted range of motion goals, repetition counts, and posture criteria.
landing.step2Desc: Position your device camera. Our local pose estimator tracks target joint angles, detects peak extension, counts completed repetitions, and offers real-time voice prompts.
landing.step3Desc: Log session pain and fatigue ratings. Review weekly activity summaries and share consent-protected progress telemetry with your treating physiotherapist.
landing.featuresSubtitle: Built with purpose-driven engineering to support safe, repeatable home exercise practice.
landing.f1Desc: 33 body landmarks estimated locally in your web browser with zero server frame uploads.
landing.f2Desc: Transparent green, red, and yellow joint highlights based on configured biomechanical criteria.
landing.f3Desc: Text-to-speech cues for movement start, hold duration, rep completion, and repositioning warnings.
landing.f4Desc: Reference instructional panels visible directly alongside your camera feed for easy comparison.
landing.f5Desc: Track daily session history, adherence trends, and repetition totals without fabricated recovery scores.
landing.f6Desc: Structured progress digests distinguishing recorded exercise data from patient-reported symptoms.
landing.f7Desc: Record pain on a standardized 0–10 scale, track fatigue, and note discomfort stops after every session.
landing.f8Desc: Consent-based sharing enabling authorized physiotherapists and family members to review progress.
landing.dualTitle: Connecting patients and clinicians between visits.
landing.dualSubtitle: Rehabilitation adherence often suffers once a patient leaves the clinic. Pysiosaathi bridges the gap by enabling clinicians to prescribe verifiable exercise programs and review transparent activity logs.
landing.forPatientsDesc: Clear guidance at home, real-time feedback to prevent second-guessing, and simple symptom logging.
landing.forTherapistsDesc: Assign tailored target angles and rep counts, review movement anomaly flags, and inspect reported pain trends.
landing.b1: We do not infer medical recovery or tissue healing from repetition counts.
landing.b2: Target ranges come from clinician-prescribed plans, never generic black-box models.
landing.b3: Uncertain or occluded angles pause the assessment rather than fabricating scores.
landing.trustSubtitle: Designed from the ground up to respect patient confidentiality and clinical safety boundaries.
landing.t1Desc: MediaPipe pose estimation runs directly on your device utilizing WebAssembly. Raw camera video frames are processed in memory and never transmitted to any cloud server.
landing.t2Desc: We do not record, store, or archive camera video by default. Only numerical movement telemetry (joint angles and rep events) is saved when you explicitly finish a session.
landing.t3Desc: Session activity summaries can only be accessed by care team members whom you have explicitly authorized. Access can be revoked instantly at any time.
landing.t4Desc: Our AI assistant strictly directs urgent symptoms (severe chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden numbness) to emergency medical services (call 112 in India).
landing.ctaTitle: Take the next step in your rehabilitation journey.
landing.ctaSubtitle: Experience guided movement tracking, clear recovery summaries, and seamless communication with your physiotherapist.
landing.footerNotice: Medical & Clinical Notice: Pysiosaathi is an assistive tool providing computer-vision movement feedback and activity tracking. It does not provide medical diagnoses, clinical validation, or self-directed alterations to prescribed regimens. Always consult with your licensed physiotherapist or medical doctor before beginning or adjusting any exercise routine.

camera.guidanceDesc: Position your device 5–6 feet away so your full body and exercising limb are visible. Video is processed locally on this device.
camera.pressEscToExit: Press Esc or click to exit full screen

exercise.seatedKneeExtDesc: Quadriceps strengthening and knee joint mobility rehabilitation exercise performed while seated upright.
exercise.shoulderAbdDesc: Deltoid and rotator cuff progressive mobility exercise lifting arm outward in the coronal plane.
instructions: Sit comfortably upright in a sturdy chair with your back supported.
Align your camera so your hip, knee, and ankle are clearly visible from the side or slight 45° angle.
Slowly straighten your lower leg until it is extended horizontally (approx. 160°–180°).
Hold the top position for 2 seconds while feeling the front thigh muscle engage.
Gently lower your foot back down under control.
exercise.unreviewedNotice: Note: Translations of exercise instructions are automated for accessibility and pending clinical review by your qualified physiotherapist.

voice.ready: Ready. Please align your knee and ankle in camera view.
voice.errorCue: Try to extend fully without slumping backward.
voice.reposition: Please adjust your position; knee landmark is obstructed.
voice.voiceFallback: Native voice synthesis for this language is simulated via closest available speech synthesizer.

progress.title: Recovery Activity & Telemetry
progress.subtitle: Detailed record of completed exercise sessions and self-reported pain levels over time.

checkin.title: Post-Session Recovery Check-in
checkin.subtitle: Help your care team understand how your body feels after exercise.
checkin.painLabel: Pain Level (0 = No Pain, 10 = Severe Pain)
checkin.stoppedEarlyLabel: I stopped early or reduced repetitions because of joint pain or acute discomfort
checkin.notesPlaceholder: e.g. Mild stiffness during initial 3 reps; eased up by rep 6.
checkin.checkinSuccessDesc: Your pain and fatigue rating have been saved to your recovery record.

chatbot.title: AI Recovery Assistant
chatbot.subtitle: Ask questions about your prescribed movements, icing protocols, and recovery hygiene.
chatbot.initialGreeting: Hello, I am your Pysiosaathi Rehabilitation Assistant. I can help clarify how to perform prescribed movements, explain general rest and icing guidelines, and answer common physical therapy questions. How can I assist your recovery today?
chatbot.inputPlaceholder: Ask a question (e.g. When should I use ice vs heat?)...
chatbot.emergencyAlertDesc: Immediate Medical Attention Required: You reported acute symptoms (e.g. severe chest pain, breathing difficulty, or sudden neurological deficits). Please seek emergency medical care immediately. Call 112 (National Emergency Helpline in India) or go to the nearest emergency room.
chatbot.emergencyWarningMsg: 🚨 URGENT SAFETY ALERT: The symptoms you described require prompt medical evaluation by emergency physicians, not routine rehabilitation advice. Please do not wait. Call 112 or contact emergency healthcare personnel immediately.
chatbot.iceAdvice: Ice is typically recommended for acute inflammation, warmth, or swelling within 24–48 hours of exercise. Mild moist heat is best used prior to stretching to relax tight muscles. Always place a cloth between the ice pack and your skin.
chatbot.repAdvice: Quality of movement is much more important than the number of repetitions. If you experience sharp pain before completing your assigned target, pause immediately and log it in your recovery check-in.
chatbot.generalAdvice: For standard post-exercise soreness, gentle elevation, resting the joint, and applying a cold compress for 15 minutes can help soothe discomfort. If soreness persists beyond 48 hours or sharp pain occurs, please notify your physiotherapist.
